question.prompt: There are integers \(a,\) \(b,\) and \(c,\) each greater than \(1,\) such that \[\sqrt[a]{N \sqrt[b]{N \sqrt[c]{N}}} = \sqrt[36]{N^{25}}\] for all \(N \gt 1.\) What is \(b?\)

solutions.title: Bound the integer indices
solutions.explanation:
Writing the nested radicals as powers of \(N\) turns the identity into an equation whose integer unknowns can be tightly bounded.

Working from the innermost radical outward gives
\[
\sqrt[a]{N\sqrt[b]{N\sqrt[c]{N}}}
=N^{\frac1a+\frac1{ab}+\frac1{abc}}.
\]
Because \(N>1\), equal powers of \(N\) have equal exponents. Therefore,
\[
\frac1a\left(1+\frac1b+\frac1{bc}\right)=\frac{25}{36}.
\]

Since \(b,c\ge2\),
\[
\frac{25a}{36}
=1+\frac1b+\frac1{bc}
\le1+\frac12+\frac14
=\frac74.
\]
Thus \(a\le\frac{63}{25}<3\). As \(a\) is an integer greater than \(1\), we must have \(a=2\).

Substituting this value and rearranging gives
\[
\frac1b+\frac1{bc}=\frac7{18},
\qquad
\frac{7b}{18}=1+\frac1c.
\]
Now \(c\ge2\), so
\[
1<\frac{7b}{18}\le\frac32,
\qquad
\frac{18}{7}<b\le\frac{27}{7}.
\]
The only integer in this interval is \(b=3\). This gives \(c=6\), and indeed
\[
\frac12+\frac16+\frac1{36}=\frac{25}{36}.
\]
Therefore, \(\boxed{b=3}\), choice \(\textbf{B}\).
